objective: Publish a release whose binaries run on the machine that downloads them, and prove it on a CPU that the previous artifacts did not support.

the_defect.summary: The v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 release tarballs were built on an AMD runner with Zig's native CPU model, so they carried SSE4a instructions, which do not exist on Intel CPUs.
the_defect.symptom: the backend CLI died with SIGILL the first time it opened a TLS connection: `calix news` and `calix search` were dead on an ordinary Arch machine
the_defect.faulting_instruction: extrq $0x8,$0x18,%xmm4 (SSE4a) in Zig's std.crypto pcurves/p256, reached from Calix.Http/src/http_client.zig

evidence.rust_note: the Rust frontend dispatches to wider implementations at runtime, so it runs on a CPU without AVX-512 or SSE4a; the Zig binaries had no such dispatch

scope: Calix.Cli.Zig, Calix.Flatpak.Backend and Calix.PackageManager resolve the x86_64 baseline CPU model instead of the build machine's
the gate disassembles every shipped binary and fails it when it uses an instruction above the baseline
the frontend moves to 0.2.2 and the release notes state plainly that v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 crash on Intel CPUs
the_fix.negative_test: a build asked for the native CPU model is caught by the gate; the default build is not

live_install.elevation: polkit only; no sudo, su or doas
live_install.live_verification: search, resolve, news, the unified inventory with 1968 packages, the daemon's inventory action and the Flatpak search all answer on the installed package

artifact_check.method: the published tarball was downloaded, its checksum verified, its binaries disassembled, and the whole tree run on the machine that found the defect
artifact_check.calix_news: No new news found (the HTTPS path that killed v0.2.0 and v0.2.1)
artifact_check.frontend: the window is mapped: at [61,1217] size [662,804]

known_gaps: The v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 release tarballs stay published and broken on Intel CPUs. The release notes of v0.2.2 say so, but the old artifacts were not withdrawn.

The Rust frontend is not covered by the portability gate: its disassembly contains instructions above the baseline, dispatched at runtime. A static check cannot tell dispatched code from straight-line code, so the gate leaves it alone and the artifact check runs it instead.
The CI cache key includes Cargo.lock, so every version bump makes the tag run a cold Rust build: this run took 16m29s against a 35-minute step timeout.
